text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify the nature of your movement disorder; are you experiencing a persistent, involuntary twisting of your neck or trunk, or is it a rapid, jerky movement? Additionally, have you noticed any rhythmic shaking or tremors in your hands or limbs while at rest?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for clarifying; these symptoms of inner restlessness and an irresistible urge to move are classic for akathisia. To confirm this diagnosis, I need to know if you have noticed any stiffness in your muscles or a resting tremor in your hands?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any muscle stiffness, a shuffling gait, or a resting tremor that would suggest parkinsonism? Also, have you noticed any facial grimacing, tongue protrusion, or other involuntary choreoathetoid movements that might indicate tardive dyskinesia?

text: Based on your description of inner restlessness and the absence of stiffness or involuntary facial movements, your symptoms are highly consistent with akathisia induced by risperidone.
